topic: q-zone: the zone_members row and the zone read it is built on
method: Framework-level evidence: the row is a query row of ForgeTrigger and reads the world only through RuntimeQuerySession. The one world read it needs — which zone an entity stands in — is not a snapshot field, so this batch added it to the framework; see ForgeMap/evidence/zone-reader.json for the native members that answer it.

reads.boundedBy: RuntimeKernel.MaximumEntityReferencesPerQuery (256) and the tick budget (64 queries, 1024 references); one query is charged per candidate, so a set read one entity at a time costs the same as the set read in one call
refusals: entity-zone-unavailable: the kind's owner registered no zone responder
entity-zone-unknown: the owner cannot place the entity right now
entity-zone-kind: the responder answered a reference that is not a zone
entity-query-tick-budget: the tick's queries are spent
stale-world / stale-entity: the reference is not current

reads.why: The row reads its own port first, so a plan naming a zone this level does not have is refused before any candidate is read; the entity it answers with is the kernel's own reference, which is what the candidates are compared against.

notVerifiedInGame: The per-tick budget behaviour of a zone filter over a full candidate set inside a real dispatch (the unit case covers 256 candidates and the budget code, but the game's own tick pacing is not exercised).
Whether the host's tick rate makes a 256-candidate zone filter cheap enough to run every frame; the row is a query step, so it is evaluated on demand and memoized per activation.
